title: Response Composition Presets — Brainlog
content:
Quick brainlog: rough PRD sketch for a small developer-facing feature that ships quickly and helps standardize how applications compose LLM responses to balance token cost, latency, and UX. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of TODOs and rough ideas.

Problem we keep seeing
- Customers and internal teams keep hand-crafting prompt templates (and whole stacks of system/user + few-shot context) for similar use cases: summaries, step-by-step guides, short answers, persona voice.
- Repetition leads to inconsistent outputs, hard-to-reuse prompts, and unpredictable token/cost profiles.
- We have existing knobs (model variant, max_tokens, temperature, stop sequences, streaming) but no standardized, sharable presets that capture composition tradeoffs (verbosity vs fidelity vs cost).

What are Response Composition Presets (RCP)?
- Small named bundles (presets) that encode a composition strategy for a response. Includes: system prompt fragment, output format constraints, length budget guidance, quality fallback policy, and optional post-processing/structure hints.
- Presets are first-class in the API + Console: developers can reference a preset id instead of copying templates.
- Presets can be parameterized (placeholders replaced at call time), versioned, and optionally pinned to model families.

Goals (MVP)
- Reduce prompt duplication and make token cost predictable for common patterns.
- Enable teams to share best-practice response blueprints across projects.
- Provide telemetry to show how presets impact cost & quality.

Non-goals (MVP)
- Not a full authoring UX with WYSIWYG templates (later). Not replacing comprehensive prompt engineering tooling.

User stories (priority order)
1) As a product engineer, I can reference a preset id when calling Redwood API so I don't have to embed the entire system prompt in my request (simple: preset=rcp:concise-summary:v1).
   - Acceptance: API accepts preset param; response follows the preset constraints (length and structure) in >80% cases on synthetic tests.
2) As a solutions engineer, I can create a preset in the Console that other teams can discover and comment on.
   - Acceptance: minimal console UX to define name, short description, format (json/text/list), length class (short/medium/long), quality fallback.
3) As an SRE, I can see preset-level telemetry: avg tokens per response, latency, error rate, and a small quality signal (human eval pass-rate or heuristic).
   - Acceptance: telemetry surfaced in Console and available via API.
4) As a compliance owner, I can restrict which presets can be used in Private deployments (whitelist).
   - Acceptance: admin can tag presets and set allowlist rules.

MVP feature surface
- API: new optional field `response_preset` (string). If present, runtime fetches preset and applies server-side pre/post processing.
- Storage: simple preset object {id, name, description, model_affinity, system_fragment, format_hint, length_bucket, fallback_policy, metadata_tags}. Keep flat.
- Console: list + create form (minimal), with versioning via new version button.
- Telemetry: per-preset aggregates (tokens_out, tokens_in, latency_p50/p95, error_count, sample_quality_score).
- SDK: tiny helpers to list presets and inject params.

Server-side behavior notes
- Server should not blindly overwrite user-provided system prompt, but apply preset fragment as a prefix or optionally replace (configurable). Default: prefix.
- Length budget enforcement: translate length_bucket into max_tokens and soft truncation hints. If model returns longer, runtime truncates to format_hint (for structured formats) or post-processes (strip trailing text).
- Fallback policy: if model confidence low (heuristic, or eval failing structure), apply lower-cost fallback preset (e.g., shorter summarizer) or return partial with a flag.

Example presets (MVP set)
- concise-summary:v1 — system fragment: "Summarize in 2 short paragraphs; prioritize clarity; do not invent facts." format_hint: "text" length: short.
- step-by-step-lite:v1 — return 3–5 numbered steps; each step max 40 tokens. fallback: bullet-list-short.
- persona-casual-brief:v1 — apply voice transforms, prefer contractions, max 120 tokens, stop sequence: "###END".

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Where do we draw the line between preset and full prompt template (few-shot examples)? Example-heavy presets can bloat storage and tokens. Maybe only allow example snippets in private/dedicated tiers.
- Safety: some presets could encourage problematic outputs (e.g., persuasive messaging). Need policy review and admin controls.
- How do we signal to the runtime which parts of response are "guaranteed" (structured fields) vs free text? We'll need a format schema in presets (lightweight, e.g., "json:{title:string,steps:array}"), which complicates runtime parsing. MVP: only support plain/text and simple line-delimited lists.

Telemetry and success metrics
- Adoption: % of new hosted API calls that pass response_preset within 12 weeks. Target: 10% org-wide within first quarter of availability for open-source customers.
- Token reduction: avg tokens per call delta vs same baseline pattern. Target: 15% reduction for concise presets.
- UX quality: for a curated eval set, preserve pass-rate within 5% vs bespoke prompt baseline.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Alpha: internal teams + a handful of partner customers. Manual provisioning of presets. Gather telemetry and iterate.
- Beta: Console create/list + public presets gallery. SDK helpers.
- GA: public API surfaced with retention/versioning and admin controls for Dedicated/Private.

Implementation risks / engineering notes
- Runtime must fetch preset fast; consider caching presets per-tenant and invalidation on update. Keep preset size small.
- Post-processing (format enforcement) will add latency; measure cost vs value. Provide option to bypass for latency-sensitive calls.
- Compatibility: map presets to model families. A preset tuned to gpt-like might behave differently on smaller LLaMA variants. Expose model_affinity to help routing.

Next steps / immediate TODOs
- Mock RFC for console UX (Jordan) — tiny wireframes + list/create page.
- Minimal API contract (Mika) — add to openapi draft for hosted API.
- Telemetry schema (me) — small protobuf/json for per-preset metrics.
- Security review checkpoint before beta (add to product-ops backlog).

Notes to self
- Keep presets small and composable. Favor small fragments + external parameterization over giant static templates.
- Think about a preset marketplace later (internal curated + community-shared).
- We should prototype 3 presets and run A/B with current hostings to see token/quality impact.

Random UX scribbles
- Console: a quick test-send tool where you pick a preset, enter example input, and see token preview + diff vs raw prompt.
- CLI: `rw presets preview --preset concise-summary:v1 --input-file example.md` returns a token estimate + sample output.

Rough wireframe links (not real):
- TODO: put sketches in Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-1234) and link screenshots.

End of brainlog. Will tidy into a short PRD if the alpha metrics look promising.
